title: Program Support Director – Francophone and Lusophone Africa
description: This position is 100% remote. Candidates may work remotely from any of the following countries: Burundi, Chad, Benin, Madagascar, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Cote d’Ivoire, Ethiopia, Kenya/Alliance locations, Malawi, Mozambique, Nigeria, South Africa, and Zambia. Candidates in West Africa are preferred. The Program Support Director (PSD) is a senior leadership position within Ipas’s Global Program Support Team. The PSD serves as strategic thought partner to the Regional Directors (RDs), Country Directors (CDs) and other leaders across the Ipas network, helping strengthen organizational effectiveness, program quality, risk management and leadership capacity. The PSD provides strategic leadership, technical guidance, and operational oversight to 4–5 regional or country programs. This role supervises 3-5 direct reports which include CDs and RDs as well as Senior Program Managers (SPMs), who are part of the global Program Support Team. Reporting to the Deputy Chief Operating Officer (DCOO), the PSD ensures alignment with Ipas strategy and quality standards, donor and award compliance, and risk mitigation. The PSD serves as a bridge between Ipas global teams and regional / country offices, promoting cross learning and providing supportive supervision and thought partnership to country team leaders. The PSD will bring significant team and program leadership experience, cross cultural knowledge, relevant language skills, a focus on user-centered approaches, and a dedication to shared leadership. The job responsibilities include working collaboratively with country program staff to ensure strong program results and strong project and risk management. The PSD provides high level stewardship and serve an “internal control” function with assigned regional and country programs, to ensure compliance with Ipas’s quality standards and as a steward of the Ipas’s global reputation. The position contributes significantly to addressing programmatic challenges and problem solving; ensuring we achieve desired goals, donor satisfaction and compliance with award terms and conditions, strengthening systems to improve value for money, organizational learning; and promoting a positive and empowering work culture. The PSD has a strong commitment to reproductive justice and Ipas’s mission. Demonstrates a strong commitment to the individuals and communities we serve, acting with a sense of urgency and providing candid timely support and guidance to their team and peers. Primary Responsibilities: Strategic Leadership Partner with regional and country leadership to advance organizational priorities, strengthen strategic decision-making, and promote alignment with Ipass mission, values, strategic framework, global standards, policies and shared leadership practices. Support leaders in monitoring organizational, programmatic, and financial performance and in addressing emerging challenges, risks, and opportunities Participate in global strategic initiatives and other organizational development efforts to strengthen the Ipas Network, such as global strategic planning, expanding implementation of shared leadership practices and risk management. Represent Ipas on national or regional Boards of Directors, as needed. Support and provide thought leadership to regional and country leadership in translating organizational strategy into high-quality, contextually relevant program strategies. Program Quality, Stewardship and Support Provide high-level strategic inputs and assistance in project and program management with a focus on addressing challenges and problem solving with assigned regional and country teams. Facilitate periodic reviews with country and regional leaders to strengthen compliance, program quality, organizational learning, and accountability towards Ipas policies and quality standards, donor requirements, local laws and regulations, and standard accounting and business practices. Lead or support special assessments or learning initiatives, as needed. Regional and Country Program Support Serve as a trusted advisor to RDs and CDs, supporting leadership effectiveness, adaptive management, and cross-organizational collaboration Provide supportive supervision and thought partnership with RDs and CDs. Promote strong communication, collaboration, and cross learning among Ipas network technical and support units, and other country programs to strengthen programmatic and operational results. Support RDs, CDs and SPMs in addressing implementation challenges, risk management, and adaptive programming. Contribute to developing/updating and implementing strong regional/country strategic plans as requested, ensuring alignment with the Ipas mission and strategic framework. Provide coaching and support to RDs and CDs in recruiting and developing a high functioning team that practices shared leadership and maintains a positive and effective work culture. Provide strategic input on annual work plans, annual operating budgets, reports, and high-priority deliverables, as requested and needed. Oversee the strengthening of a variety of mechanisms to support a positive and effective work culture, organizational learning, sharing, and peer support across teams. Support start-up, scale-up, and close-out of country programs. Staff Management & Capacity Strengthening Foster a culture of shared leadership, accountability, learning, trust, and inclusion by empowering staff to contribute expertise, exercise leadership, and make informed decisions appropriate to their roles. Provide supportive supervision and manage the performance of direct reports, including RDs, CDs and Program Support Team staff. Support capacity strengthening of regional/country teams in program management, donor compliance and risk management. Promote organizational training and other capacity strengthening efforts as needed. Donor Engagement & Compliance Support RDs and CDs in managing complex donor-funded portfolios by strengthening systems, decision-making, compliance practices, and cross-node coordination. Ensure programs comply with donor requirements and organizational policies. Contribute to resource mobilization efforts by contributing to proposal development, donor briefings, and strategic partnerships as requested and needed. Work with program leaders to ensure that new business efforts and proposals are aligned with the country/region’s strategic plan, Ipas strategic framework, technical excellence and innovation, good stewardship of funding, and optimal cost recovery. Represent Ipas in donor meetings, technical forums, and external engagements as required. Risk Management & Safeguarding Ensure timely identification and mitigation of programmatic, operational, and reputational risks, working with country/regional program leaders. Promote safeguarding, protection from sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA), and ethical programming across all supported programs. Conduct regular reviews and work with country / regional leaders to ensure adherence with organizational policies on safeguarding, gender equality, and inclusion. Guard Ipas interests and reputation through oversight on adherence to policies, performance against the annual operating budget, addressing audit findings and ethical issues, and compliance with donor requirements. Work closely with regional and country leaders and other Ipas units to ensure adequate internal controls to reduce the risk of fraud and mismanagement of funds; Play an internal control function where needed, such as to reduce perceived or actual conflicts of interest. Monitoring, Evaluation, Learning & Accountability (MEL) Promote strong monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning practices across assigned regional and country programs. Support the use of data for decision-making, learning, and program improvement. Encourage documentation of best practices, innovations, and lessons learned across all projects. Minimum Requirements: Essential Commitment to sexual and reproductive health and rights, especially safe abortion and access to contraception, and an understanding of principles, policies, and best practices related to sexual and reproductive health, and related intersectionalities. Knowledge of the issues and context of womens sexual and reproductive health and rights in the Africa region, including demonstrated experience working with NGOs in Africa, preferably having worked in an Ipas implementing country in the West Africa region. Demonstrated commitment to shared leadership principles, with experience fostering distributed leadership, collaboration, accountability, and trust across geographically dispersed teams Proven ability to lead and motivate teams and create a positive work environment through supportive supervision, strong communication and teamwork, and shared leadership approaches, including demonstrated successes in program management, team leadership, strategic planning and problem solving. Proven ability to build and maintain positive working relationships with a variety of partners, including government officials, regional or global donors and partner organizations. Ability to work across cultures and manage complex relationships remotely. Minimum At least 15 years of increasing responsibility in non-profit leadership and program management in the international development or NGO-sector. Minimum of 7 years of senior program leadership experience overseeing multiple country programs and proven ability to provide strategic and technical leadership across diverse country contexts. Strong experience managing donor-funded programs (e.g., bilateral, multilateral, foundations) including budgetary management. Demonstrated experience supporting organizational risk management, compliance monitoring, and implementation of internal control systems Relevant post-graduate degree (e.g., MBA, MIA, MPH). Respect and credibility as an advocate for reproductive health and rights Strong written and verbal communication skills in English. Fluency in French required. Knowledge of Portuguese will be an added advantage and of other local languages will be an asset. Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, PowerPoint, Word, SharePoint, etc. Travel Requirements: Estimated 20 %-25 % time travel t o regional and country programs and regional/global meetings. Compensation for this position will be determined by the prevailing market rate in the employees country and the applicable statutory laws, in addition to Ipass own pay philosophy and other factors, such as the employees experience level and expertise. Ipas is strongly committed to providing a work environment that is free from all forms of harassment, discrimination, and inequity. title: Director, Strategic Portfolio
description: Ipas is a global reproductive justice organization working to ensure that all people can exercise their right to bodily autonomy and access quality abortion and contraception services. We work hand in hand with governments, civil society, health systems, and communities. Ipas advances sustainable abortion ecosystems that expand access, reduce stigma, improve quality of care, and strengthen supportive policy and financing environments to make care possible, permanently. This is a remote position. Compensation for this position will be determined by the prevailing market rate in the employee's country in addition to Ipas's own pay philosophy and other factors, such as the employee's experience level and expertise. Candidates can expect traveling up to 30% time. Candidates based in the following countries are eligible to apply: Bangladesh, Bolivia, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Cote d’Ivoire, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Kenya/Alliance locations, Malawi, Mexico, Mozambique, Nepal, Nigeria, Pakistan, South Africa, Zambia, United Kingdom and Europe. This role is grounded in and informs the Ipas strategy and evidence/measurement of impact. The Director will provide strategic technical leadership, coordination, and relationship management for Ipas’s engagement with high investment donor(s) and other key partnerships, as needed. This is a leadership role — for someone who can hold the strategic vision, build trust and partnership with funders, partners, governments and movements, mobilise country teams, and translate complex implementation into insight and narrative that drives organizational learning and continued investment. You will work closely with Ipas’s most senior leaders and be a visible external presence for the organisation. This role requires a highly strategic leader with strong political acumen, partnership management skills, methodological rigor, systems thinking capability, and experience navigating complex, multi-stakeholder reproductive health and development initiatives. Primary responsibilities: Lead a Strategic Portfolio Own the strategic coordination and technical excellence of a large and complex portfolio, ensuring alignment and integrating learning with the organizational strategy Support the design of integrated approaches that expand abortion and contraception access through health systems strengthening policy engagement, financing, community support, and stigma reduction. Drive alignment between organizational strategy, donor priorities , key partnerships and country implementation, identifying opportunities for scale, learning and innovation, financing and systems change. Contribute to country and regional project design, ensure coherence across the Ipas global portfolio Lead the Ipas relationship with Selected Donors/Partners Serve as a primary relationship manager for key donor portfolios , in collaboration with senior Ipas leadership L eading donor communications, updates, learning engagements, and strategic discussions to ensure that Ipas is always responsive, credible and forward looking Ensure internal communication and understanding of emerging shifts and priority decisions Ensure high-quality donor and partnership stewardship, responsiveness, and confidence. Produce high-quality, evidence-driven strategic briefs, presentations, reports, and donor-facing materials that reflect both ambition and rigorous delivery Coordinate donor visits, learning exchanges, and portfolio reviews. Ensure Excellent Technical and Program Delivery Work closely with technical and country teams to ensure quality implementation and adaptive management across the portfolio. Facilitate cross-country learning and embed emerging evidence into programming in real time. Facilitate collaboration across clinical, community, policy, financing, evidence, and advocacy workstreams. Support development of impact measurement, implementation frameworks, partnership models, and systems-level approaches that strengthen sustainable abortion ecosystems. Ensure the needs of women and girls, including adolescents, remain central, addressed through practical, rights-based approaches. Strengthen the Ecosystem Around the Work Cultivate strategic relationships with governments, civil society organizations, youth-led groups, philanthropic actors, multilateral agencies, and research institutions. Position Ipas as a thought leader in abortion and contraception access, reproductive justice, and sustainable abortion ecosystem approaches. Support convenings, external engagement opportunities, and collaborative partnerships. Identify co-funding and partnership opportunities aligned with the portfolio. Drive Evidence, Learning, and Adaption Support learning agendas, portfolio reviews, and evidence generation efforts, working with MEL and technical teams to strengthen outcome tracking and systems-level measurement. Translate implementation learning into strategic insights for internal and external audiences. Champion adaptive management across country portfolios, building a culture of continuous improvement. Other duties as assigned. Minimum requirements: Advanced degree in public health, international development, gender studies, social sciences, public policy, or related field. 10–15 years of progressively senior experience in international development, SRHR, gender equality, adolescent health, philanthropy, or systems strengthening. Experienced with impact measurement, evidence-driven adaptive programming and communicating results Deep understanding of abortion access, contraception, reproductive justice, SRHR, strengthening health systems policy advocacy, and gender equality-including the political landscape that shapes this work Demonstrated experience managing complex multi country donor portfolios, particularly with large philanthropic funders. Strong political acumen and the ability to navigate sensitive, multi-stakeholder environments with confidence and care. Excellent communication, facilitation, and presentation skills- you can distill complex evidence into a compelling narrative for any audience. Experience supporting ecosystem or systems-change approaches, particularly in low- and middle-income countries A collaborative, adaptive leadership style — you bring people together across functions and geographies and build trust quickly. Competencies: What We’re Looking For You’re a senior leader with deep SRHR or global health experience who thrives at the intersection of strategy, evidence, relationships, and delivery. You’re comfortable with ambiguity, energised by complexity, and genuinely committed to reproductive justice. Organizational‑level strategic thinking and results stewardship. Decisive, values‑grounded risk management. Feminist leadership and shared power practice. Complex stakeholder and donor relationship management. Systems integration, learning, and adaptive leadership. Clear, credible communication in high‑ambiguity environments. Working environment: This position is fully remote, subject to change based on business need. Flexibility to meet virtually in different time zones required. title: Enterprise Risk Management Analyst
description: This position may work remotely from any of the following countries: Bangladesh, Bolivia, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Cote d’Ivoire, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Kenya/Alliance locations, Malawi, Mexico, Mozambique, Nepal, Nigeria, Pakistan, South Africa, the United Kingdom, and Zambia. Compensation for this position will be determined on the prevailing market rate in the employee's country and the applicable statutory laws, in addition to Ipas's own pay philosophy and other factors, such as the employee's experience level and expertise. The Ipas Network Risk Service Node is responsible for supporting and providing resources in the areas of risk management, safety and security, internal audit, and ethics. The Enterprise Risk Management Analyst plays a critical role in strengthening organizational resilience and accountability for Ipas in these areas. This position provides technical and operational support to the Network Risk function, which oversees enterprise risk management (ERM), safety and security, insurance and risk pooling arrangements, internal audit coordination and ethics. The Enterprise Risk Management Analyst identifies and manages threats to an organization's strategic mission, staff safety, and programmatic impact, especially in areas where complex and/or evolving legal, political, and operational landscapes create higher risk for the organization. In addition, the role supports implementation of the organization’s risk management framework to ensure Ipas can effectively identify, assess, and mitigate risks affecting program delivery, donor compliance, safeguarding commitments, and strategic objectives in diverse and often complex operating environments. Risk Identification & Assessment Conduct risk assessments considering political, regulatory, financial, and reputational factors in global operations. Identify knowledge gaps among staff and partners on risk, reporting, and organizational accountability Develop tracking mechanisms to ensure compliance with policies across all offices. Provide analysis and recommendations to inform risk mitigation plans across country offices and global teams. Collaborate with the Network Risk Director in identifying digital and physical risk indicators, ensuring that these are managed under one unified strategy. Partner with the Network Risk Director and BAM/IT Director to ensure physical security protocols (e.g., office access) align with digital security standards (e.g., server room protection). Risk Monitoring, Data Analysis Maintain and update the enterprise risk register and dashboards, synthesizing operational, financial, and security data while incorporating technical risk summaries provided by the Network Risk Director. Use data visualization tools to communicate complex risk information effectively to non-technical audiences. Prepare risk reports for senior leadership, board committees, and donors, highlighting key exposures and mitigation progress. Ensure risk management practices align with donor requirements, international standards, and local regulations in countries of operation. Collaborate with internal audit and program compliance teams to address risk-based findings. Network and Staff Safety & Security Analyze risk trends across advocacy, funding, and operational areas to inform strategic planning. Create and facilitate a network Community of Practice to strengthen safety and security within Ipas implementing areas and across the Ipas Network. Support teams by collaborating with local HR and Risk contact to coordinate resources such as EAP crisis management when facing adverse safety and/or security concerns. Capacity Building & Awareness Deliver trainings during onboarding, refresher cycles, and targeted learning sessions tailored to diverse audiences and local context. Collaborate with HR, Procurement, IT, and Communications teams to integrate risk and accountability into organizational systems. Other duties as assigned. Minimum Bachelors degree in risk management, Finance, International Development, Public Health, or related field. 5 years’ experience in enterprise risk management, compliance, or internal audit, ideally within NGOs or donor-funded projects. Proven experience creating and leading training programs Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Excellent verbal, auditory, and written communication and stakeholder engagement abilities across diverse cultural contexts and various levels of the organization. Ability to clearly and thoroughly present data through various collection sources (reports, risk registers, risk database) to key stakeholders, either through ad-hoc meetings or regularly scheduled trainings Anticipating needs of the organization and programmatic teams proactively through ongoing research and best practice knowledge Strong integrity and ability to coordinate sensitive matters with discretion, confidentiality, and neutrality. Proficiency in risk management tools and data visualization platforms, such as Power BI. Preferred Skills: Familiarity with reproductive health programs and global advocacy environments is highly desirable. Strong verbal, auditory, and written communication skills in any language that is frequently used by Ipas employees (French, Portuguese, Spanish, Hindi, etc.) Certification in Risk Management Core Competencies Commitment to reproductive justice and gender equity principles. Strategic thinking and ability to connect risk insights to mission-driven objectives. Cultural sensitivity and adaptability in global contexts. High ethical standards and integrity.
